subject: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 4:18 PM
Subject: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)
Attachments: KMS_Wrapper_Rollout_GoNoGo_Checklist_v3.docx; KMS_Rollout_Risk_Assessment_2025-11-12.pdf

Aisha, Naomi —

Before we take the new standardized KMS client wrapper past staging, I want leadership-level alignment on rollout risk, mitigations, and explicit go/no-go criteria.

What’s changing
- Standard KMS wrapper with enforced timeouts + retry budgets + error mapping (ref: redwood#18421, #18502)
- Circuit breaker + degrade-mode behavior to prevent cascades during KMS incidents (ref: redwood#18449)
- Healthcheck endpoint + pre-deploy hooks (ref: redwood#18527)

Primary risks we need to be crisp about
1) Retry amplification / “storm” against KMS under partial timeouts
   - Impact: KMS throttling, elevated p95/p99 latency, request pileups
2) Incorrect failure classification (e.g., treating AccessDenied like transient)
   - Impact: hides real misconfig, prolongs incident, potential data-plane unavailability
3) Unexpected “strictness” change in prod (timeouts too low, breaker too aggressive)
   - Impact: avoidable decrypt failures / 5xx increases
4) Rotation corner cases (dual-read window and caching semantics)
   - Impact: decrypt mismatch, stuck partial cutover states

Mitigations in place / planned
- Hard caps on retries and total elapsed time; config guardrails require explicit override for prod (redwood#18502)
- Circuit breaker with jitter/backoff and bounded half-open probing; documented degrade policy (redwood#18449)
- Standardized error taxonomy + actionable logs (AccessDenied vs Throttling vs Timeout) (in flight under ENG-4822)
- Feature flag / kill switch for wrapper enablement per service + per region
- Canary + staged rollout: staging soak -> prod canary (us-east) -> expand by region

What I need from you
1) Confirmation the go/no-go criteria is sufficient for security/compliance + enterprise expectations.
2) Decision: do we require explicit SRE sign-off (Sean/Rafael) before prod canary, or do we treat that as part of the release checklist without leadership gating?

Proposed rollout plan (draft)
- Wed/Thu: staging enablement + 24h soak
- Fri: prod canary 1% (us-east), hold 4h, then 10% for remainder of day
- Next business day: expand to 50% then 100% if stable

Proposed go/no-go criteria (high level)
- No sustained increase in service-level 5xx attributable to KMS (<= +0.03% absolute over baseline during canary window)
- KMS wrapper p95 latency within +20ms of baseline (per region) and p99 within +50ms
- Circuit breaker trip rate < 0.5% of KMS calls during canary; no prolonged open state > 2 min without corresponding known KMS incident
- No increase in AccessDenied errors (should remain at baseline; any increase is a stop + investigate)
- Dashboards + alerts live and not paging noisily in staging

If you’re aligned, I’ll ask the platform team to produce an SRE sign-off note that explicitly references dashboards/alerts and rollback triggers.

Priya
—
Priya Natarajan
Platform Exec Sponsor
Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 5:02 PM
Subject: Re: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)

Priya —

+1 to making the criteria explicit. From the customer expectation / enterprise review angle, two additions I’d like to see baked in:

1) Change management / comms
- For Dedicated/Private customers: we should be able to say “no behavior change unless enabled / configured,” and document what “degrade mode” means in plain language (what fails closed vs fails open, and what operators will observe).
- For hosted: we need an internal FAQ snippet for SE/Sales in case canary causes questions (“Why did KMS errors appear in logs?” etc.).

2) Evidence & auditability
- Rotation/cutover toggles should generate audit log events (even if customer never sees them in hosted) so we can answer “who/when” during security reviews.

On SRE sign-off: for something that can cascade across regions, I recommend we make it an explicit gate for prod canary. It’s cheaper than a rollback + customer comms.

If you want, I can draft a one-pager that ties the go/no-go to “what auditors ask” + the operator-facing narrative.

Naomi
Product — Security & Compliance



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 6:11 PM
Subject: Re: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)

Agree with the approach and strongly agree on explicit SRE sign-off as a release gate.

Security-specific go/no-go items I want added (even if they’re “should be no-op”):
- Confirm logs do not contain plaintext key material / decrypted data under any error path (including debug-level logs in staging).
- Confirm AccessDenied / NotFound are treated as non-retryable and bubble with actionable messaging (this is a frequent enterprise pain point).
- Confirm caching semantics are bounded and do not allow stale key metadata across rotations (esp. during dual-read windows). I don’t need new primitives, but I do need us to be able to explain “how we avoid stale reads” in a review.

On failure policy: the degrade-mode behavior needs one crisp sentence we can reuse across materials. Example: “If KMS is degraded, the system stops encrypting new material and surfaces a clear error rather than repeatedly retrying and impacting availability.” (We can tune this based on the exact behavior, but we need the narrative aligned.)

Finally: please ensure the sign-off explicitly references (a) dashboards, (b) paging thresholds, and (c) rollback criteria. If we’re using kill switches, include who is authorized to flip them.

Aisha
—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Exec Sponsor, Security
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 13, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Re: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)

Thanks — I’m going to make SRE sign-off an explicit gate for prod canary.

Updates I’m making to the go/no-go + release checklist (based on your notes):

Additions (Security)
- Verify no sensitive payloads in logs (include a spot-check procedure + sampling query for staging)
- Explicit non-retryable classification: AccessDenied / NotFound / InvalidCiphertext => no retries; stop + surface actionable error
- Cache/rotation safety statement: cache TTLs + invalidation behavior documented; no stale key metadata beyond TTL; dual-read window has deterministic precedence and rollback toggle

Additions (Product / customer narrative)
- One sentence for “degrade mode” behavior that matches actual implementation
- Internal SE FAQ snippet prepared before prod canary
- Audit log events for cutover toggles/rotation-related changes tracked as a hard requirement (I’ll ensure this is part of the release scope)

Rollout sequencing (more conservative)
- Staging enablement + 24h soak (minimum)
- Prod canary 1% (us-east) with a 2h hold and explicit checkpoint
- Expand to 10% (same region) for remainder of day
- Next day: expand to additional region(s) only after SRE confirms alert noise is acceptable

Rollback triggers (explicit)
- +0.03% absolute 5xx increase sustained for >10 min correlated with KMS wrapper metrics
- Circuit breaker open state >2 min in canary service (without known KMS provider incident)
- Any increase in AccessDenied rate (stop, investigate config change)

Action items
- I’ll ask the platform owner to send an SRE sign-off note (Sean/Rafael) with references to dashboards + paging thresholds + who can flip kill switches.
- Naomi: if you can send the SE FAQ snippet outline today, we’ll wire it into the release comms.

Priya



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 13, 2025 at 10:07 AM
Subject: Re: KMS wrapper rollout: risk review + go/no-go criteria (request)

Works for me.

I’ll send the SE FAQ snippet + the customer-facing phrasing for degrade mode by EOD. I’ll also add one line re: “audit log events for rotation/cutover toggles” as a checklist item we can point to in enterprise reviews.

No further objections as long as SRE sign-off is a hard gate and the rollback triggers are documented in the release thread.

Naomi
